summary: Almost everyone entering Tuvalu gets a visa on arrival at Funafuti for up to one month — free for Commonwealth and Pacific nationals, AUD 100 for most others — while EU, EEA, Swiss, Serbian and Taiwanese passport holders are visa-exempt for 90 days.

AF.notes: A visa is issued on arrival at Funafuti for a stay of up to one month, against a fee usually quoted at AUD 100 in cash, a passport valid 6 months, an onward ticket, booked accommodation and proof of funds. Some official sources describe this simply as visa-free entry for 30 days — either way the permission is granted at the airport.

fee.notes: Commonly quoted at AUD 100 and waived for Commonwealth and Pacific nationalities. Carry Australian dollars in cash, as cards cannot be used at the airport.

source.name: Government of Tuvalu — visa on arrival

passportValidity.text: All visitors need a passport valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Tuvalu.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information
Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Tuvalu itself is free of yellow fever and malaria, though dengue outbreaks occur.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but Princess Margaret Hospital on Funafuti is the only facility in the country and anything serious means an evacuation flight to Fiji — comprehensive coverage with medical evacuation is strongly advised.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required for the visa on arrival, and matters in practice, since Funafuti is served by only a handful of flights a week from Suva.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must show sufficient funds and a confirmed place to stay. There are only a few guesthouses and one hotel on Funafuti, so book before you fly and bring the confirmation.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

declarations.name: Arrival and customs declaration card
declarations.text: A paper immigration and customs arrival card is completed at Funafuti International Airport, where formalities take place in a single small terminal building.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

currencyLimits.text: Significant amounts of cash must be declared on arrival and departure under Tuvalu's customs and anti-money-laundering rules. Confirm the current threshold with Customs before traveling with large sums.

source.name: Tuvalu High Commission — visa and entry information

notes: Tuvalu uses the Australian dollar alongside its own coins. Bring AUD cash, as there are no ATMs and cards are almost never accepted.
Biosecurity rules apply to fresh food, seeds, plants and animal products; declare everything on the arrival card.
Firearms and ammunition are prohibited, and drug offenses carry severe penalties.

payments.text: Tuvalu is effectively a cash economy: there are no ATMs, the National Bank of Tuvalu is the only bank, and card payments are accepted almost nowhere. Bring all the Australian dollars you will need, including the visa fee, in cash.

safety.text: Crime is very rare and Funafuti is a small, close-knit community where visitors are quickly known. The real risks are practical: no hospital beyond a basic one, very limited flights, and a low-lying atoll exposed to king tides and storm surge.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Tuvalu travel information

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is drier and less humid, with lower risk of tropical storms and king tides than the November-to-April wet season.

tips.text: There are no ATMs anywhere in Tuvalu and cards are essentially useless. Arrive with enough Australian dollars in cash for your visa, accommodation, food and departure tax-inclusive extras — running out is not easily fixed.

Funafuti is reached only by a few Fiji Airways flights a week from Suva, and they are regularly delayed or canceled. Build several buffer days into your plans and check whether you need a Fiji transit or entry permission.

Accommodation on Funafuti amounts to one hotel and a handful of guesthouses, often full with government and aid visitors. Book and reconfirm before you fly. You will be asked where you are staying on arrival.
The runway doubles as the island's main public space for football, volleyball and evening strolls; a siren clears it before each flight. Join in, but move promptly when the siren sounds.
Fresh water comes from rainwater tanks and is precious. Use it sparingly, drink bottled or boiled water, and be mindful that supplies run low in dry spells.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tuvalu?
faq.answer: Practically everyone can get one on arrival at Funafuti for a stay of up to one month, so no advance application is normally needed. Commonwealth and Pacific nationals — including the UK, Malaysia, South Korea, Fiji, Kenya and the Caribbean Commonwealth — pay nothing, most other nationalities pay a fee usually quoted at AUD 100, and EU, EEA, Swiss, Serbian and Taiwanese passport holders are visa-exempt for 90 days.

faq.question: How much does the Tuvalu visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: It is free for Commonwealth and Pacific nationalities and commonly quoted at AUD 100 for everyone else. There are no card facilities at the airport, so bring the fee in Australian dollars in cash and confirm the current amount with your airline or Tuvalu Immigration before you fly.

faq.question: How do I get to Tuvalu?
faq.answer: Almost all visitors fly Fiji Airways from Suva to Funafuti, a route that operates only a few times a week and is weather-dependent. There are no other scheduled passenger air links, so plan generous connection buffers and check Fiji's own transit requirements.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than a month?
faq.answer: Yes, in principle. Apply to the Immigration Department on Funafuti before your permitted stay expires; extensions are granted at their discretion, typically month by month, and you will need your passport, onward ticket and proof of funds.

faq.question: Are there ATMs or card payments in Tuvalu?
faq.answer: No ATMs, and card acceptance is close to non-existent. The National Bank of Tuvalu can sometimes help with cash advances, but you should not rely on it. Bring all the Australian dollars you need for the trip.
